clue.text: Players on contract have control over money

indicators.note: placed after: the players come on (following) the word for contract

parts.note: to purse the lips is to contract or pucker them
the strings are the string players of an orchestra

explanation.surface: Musicians signed to a deal turn out to hold the band's finances.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever holds the purse strings decides how the funds are spent.

clue.text: Sort! of stone, say, by northern stream

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Sort of stone, say, by northern stream' (scan agrees): BECK is the northern stream, but no clue word gives PUR, so the wordplay is incomplete.
annotationWithheld.clue: Sort! of stone, say, by northern stream

clue.text: Rung for a sandwich

explanation.surface: Someone rang up to order lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladder's step is called this, and a sandwich made from two whole slices of bread is also one.

clue.text: Cook took charge of this enterprise

explanation.surface: A chef ran a business venture.
explanation.walkthrough: Cook is Captain James Cook, whose ship on his first Pacific voyage was HMS Endeavour, not a kitchen cook.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Cook commanded the ship of that name, and an enterprise is an undertaking or attempt.

clue.text: Spell Michaelmas for example

explanation.surface: A brief period around late September.
explanation.walkthrough: Michaelmas is the autumn session at British universities and schools, named after the feast of St Michael.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell is a period of time, and Michaelmas is the name of the autumn academic session at Oxford and Cambridge.

clue.text: Risk keeping a beard?

indicators.note: the verb for risk holds the letter A inside it, as a container keeps its contents

parts.note: to imperil something is to put it at risk

explanation.surface: Is growing facial hair a gamble?
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts A inside IMPERIL. The question mark flags that the beard is a particular style.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pointed tuft under the lower lip, as worn by Napoleon III, is called by this name.

clue.text: Information on middle of the road in city

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the central two letters of the word road are taken

explanation.surface: Traffic news about the middle of the road in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Genoa is a port city in north-west Italy.

clue.text: Zero at Greenwich? One can only imagine it!

definitions.text: Zero at Greenwich? One can only imagine it!

parts.words: Zero at Greenwich? One can only imagine it!
parts.note: the zero line of longitude runs through Greenwich, and such a line exists only on maps, never on the ground

explanation.surface: A puzzle about nothing at Greenwich that exists only in the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The prime line of longitude, zero degrees, passes through Greenwich and is an imaginary line.

clue.text: Writer, not French, shows the flag

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement
non is French for no or not

explanation.surface: An author who refuses to be French waves a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow tapering banner flown from a lance or masthead goes by this name.

clue.text: Forty minutes' journey for Robin Goodfellow

definitions.text: Forty minutes' journey for Robin Goodfellow

parts.words: Forty minutes' journey for Robin Goodfellow
parts.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream Puck boasts he will put a girdle about the earth in forty minutes, a circuit returning to its start

explanation.surface: How long a sprite's trip takes.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Goodfellow is Puck, the mischievous fairy in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey out and back again, like Puck's circuit of the globe.

clue.text: Female kind about egghead

indicators.note: the word for kind goes around the letter, as about means surrounding

parts.note: nice means kind or pleasant
the head of egg is its first letter

explanation.surface: A gentle woman cares for an intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual but gives the head letter of egg, E, which 'about' puts inside NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a female relative.

clue.text: Attract close attention

parts.note: the close of something is its end
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: Draw people in by listening carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: To win someone's affection is to draw or attract them to you.

clue.text: The universe as shown by a model, perhaps

explanation.surface: Everything there is, displayed on a catwalk.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmos as made by God is the world brought into being, and a new fashion design worn by a model is a designer's work of that name.

clue.text: Kneel around Chinese cooking pot, facing the west

indicators.note: turned around, so the pan's name is read backwards

parts.note: a wok is a bowl-shaped Chinese pan
facing a direction is turned to it
W is the abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: A cook bows down beside a wok turned toward the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal but here it means turned around; 'facing' is a preposition, 'to', and 'the west' is just its abbreviated compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese gesture of deep respect involves kneeling and touching the forehead to the ground.

clue.text: Bird painter

explanation.surface: An artist known for painting birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Several songbirds are called whistlers, and James McNeill Whistler was the American painter of 'Whistler's Mother'.

clue.text: Sort of camel train out, with taxi back

indicators.note: the taxi word runs backwards, as if going back

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of train are put out of order

explanation.surface: A camel caravan is out of action, so a taxi is taken home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CAB into BAC; 'out' rearranges TRAIN into TRIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-humped camel of Central Asia is named after Bactria, an ancient region there.

clue.text: Aristocratic and well up in the Cabinet

explanation.surface: A noble who is a senior government minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' suggests government, but it is the furniture: the highest of its drawers.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper-class people are described with this term, and literally it is the highest drawer in a chest or cabinet.

clue.text: Over-indulged in the club having eaten

parts.note: a spoon was an old wooden golf club with a lofted face
fed means having been given food

explanation.surface: Someone who ate too much at the club got spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: A spoon is an old name for a golf club, roughly today's three-wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pampered and given everything without effort is figuratively fed from a spoon like a baby.

clue.text: Group of three characters speaking as one

definitions.text: Group of three characters speaking as one

parts.words: Group of three characters speaking as one
parts.note: characters are written letters, not actors, and three of them together stand for a single spoken sound

explanation.surface: A trio of actors delivering lines in chorus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' suggests people in a play; here they are letters, as in 'sch' in German.
explanation.definitionFit: Three letters representing one sound, as 'eau' in French, form this kind of letter group.

clue.text: Pain making one double up, for example

parts.note: a twin is a double or counterpart

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: An ache that bends one over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns EG into GE in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden sharp pang is the kind of pain meant.

clue.text: Odds on getting half a page of absorbing stuff

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the odds offered at the start of a race

indicators.note: the second half of the word page is taken

explanation.surface: A gambler bets on reading half a page of gripping material.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, starting price, is a horse-racing term for the odds at the off.
explanation.definitionFit: A porous material that soaks up liquid is this.

clue.text: Causes trouble about novice being the Prince of Verona

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the letter for novice
trouble suggests the letters of causes are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A ruler who stirs up a rookie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges CAUSES into ESCAUS, and 'about' puts it around L.
explanation.definitionFit: In Romeo and Juliet the ruler of Verona who banishes Romeo is named Escalus.

clue.text: Picture of scene inside house up-country

explanation.surface: A painting of a room in a rural house.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting showing the inside of a room is so called, and the inland region of a country away from the coast is also so called.

clue.text: Gamekeeper curtailed in scope

indicators.note: cut short, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a ranger looks after a park or forest and its game

explanation.surface: A gamekeeper's reach is limited.
explanation.definitionFit: Range and scope both mean the extent or reach of something.

clue.text: Judge is decisive — not a novice

indicators.note: the following letters are excluded from the word for decisive

parts.note: a critical moment is a decisive one
A plus L, the learner

explanation.surface: A judge who is decisive is no beginner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes A and L (a novice) from CRITICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A reviewer who assesses work is a judge of its merit.

clue.text: Subject vital to the memory test

indicators.note: the word lies within, at the heart of, the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A topic essential to a recall exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vital to' signals the letters lie inside 'the memory'.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic or main idea is the subject of a work.

clue.text: Check after girl leaves the country

indicators.note: the girl departs, so her letters come out of the word for check

parts.note: a perusal is a careful reading or checking
Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally

explanation.surface: Once the girl has gone, a check is made of the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Peru is a South American nation.

clue.text: Flourishing though not mature yet

explanation.surface: Thriving though still young.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush vegetation is described as verdant in this way, and an inexperienced or unripe thing is also called this colour.

clue.text: Go down hill after ending engagement

definitions.text: Go down hill after ending engagement

parts.words: Go down hill after ending engagement
parts.note: engagement here is of a gear, not of marriage: coasting downhill with the drive disengaged

explanation.surface: Things go downhill once the betrothal is broken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagement' suggests a broken romance, but a cyclist or driver disengages the gears and coasts.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast without pedalling or power, the wheels turning freely of the drive.

clue.text: Focal point for top news

parts.note: the head is the top
N, E, W and S are the four quarters or compass points

explanation.surface: Where the leading stories are gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'news' is read as the compass points N, E, W, S, which are quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: The central base of an organisation is its main centre of operations.
